title: OAuth/Policy Error: "Tool execution denied by policy" prevents basic read/write tool usage

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a clear, detailed bug report with reproduction environment (Windows PowerShell, CLI v0.37.1, OAuth auth), expected vs actual behavior, and error details ('Tool execution denied by policy').
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: Investigating and fixing policy engine denial error reporting and interactive/TTY detection behavior on Windows PowerShell requires cross-package modifications in packages/core and packages/cli, as well as testing across non-interactive policy edge cases.

summary.problem: Tool execution fails with generic 'Tool execution denied by policy' error on Windows PowerShell / non-interactive CLI environments, blocking basic file read/write and shell operations without actionable policy guidance or approval prompts.
summary.root_cause: When TTY detection flags the environment as non-interactive (e.g. in Windows PowerShell streams or wrapped invocation), `isHeadlessMode()` in `packages/core/src/utils/headless.ts` forces non-interactive mode. The policy engine matches the Headless Denial Rule in `write.toml` or default denial rules, and `getPolicyDenialError()` in `packages/core/src/scheduler/policy.ts` returns a generic 'Tool execution denied by policy' error without explaining why the policy denied execution or how to resolve it.
summary.context: Users executing CLI commands in PowerShell or headless setups encounter policy denials instead of user confirmation prompts or clear error diagnostics explaining approval mode or TTY restrictions.

steps: Enhance `getPolicyDenialError` in `packages/core/src/scheduler/policy.ts` to output detailed, actionable error messages indicating the matching rule, deny reason, and approval mode settings when tool execution is denied by policy.
Update `checkPolicy` in `packages/core/src/scheduler/policy.ts` and `policy-engine.ts` to provide clearer diagnostic context when non-interactive/headless mode blocks interactive tool confirmation.

Refine headless TTY detection in `packages/core/src/utils/headless.ts` and `packages/cli/src/config/config.ts` to prevent false-positive non-interactive flags on Windows terminals or PowerShell environments.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When tool execution is denied by policy, the CLI outputs an informative error message specifying the policy rule or non-interactive restriction causing the denial, and interactive sessions accurately allow user confirmation requests.
verification_steps: Add unit tests in `packages/core/src/scheduler/policy.test.ts` verifying that `getPolicyDenialError` includes rule deny messages and approval mode context when tool calls are denied.
Add policy engine tests verifying correct error behavior under non-interactive/headless configurations.
